interpretation: Both studies show large within-study gains. Absolute gains in the cited SkillCommit configuration are larger; current-study gains consume much of the distance from its higher starting F1 to the theoretical 100 reference.
limits: Different data difficulty, supplied prerequisites, public answer interface, executor, thinking mode and teacher are not controlled across these studies.

Gain divided by 100 minus baseline is an illustrative F1-scale normalization, not a factual error-reduction rate, an official metric, actual oracle ceiling, new significance test or proof of method superiority.
The ongoing same-condition fixed SkillCommit adaptation, not this arithmetic, provides the relevant method comparison.
